subject.title: refactor: remove browser and codex dead exports

question: After rebasing, should the combined browser/Codex export cleanup and LOC-ratchet drift repair land together, or should the automation change or ambiguous export removals be split into narrower reviews?
rationale: The branch combines a very broad API-shaped cleanup with CI-ratchet semantics, carries a protected maintainer label, and requires explicit ownership of external compatibility and final conflict resolution.

options.title: Audit, rebase, and land together
options.body: Resolve conflicts, complete the barrel/Codex/canonical-test audit, add live smoke proof, and retain the coordinated cleanup when every removed surface is confirmed private.

options.title: Split ambiguous surfaces
options.body: Land only clearly private browser and Codex removals, moving the LOC-ratchet repair or uncertain exports into focused pull requests with narrower proof.

options.title: Pause the broad cleanup
options.body: Close or defer the branch if the contract audit and conflict resolution cost outweigh the dead-export reduction.

recommendation.title: Audit, rebase, and land together
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts, complete the barrel/Codex/canonical-test audit, add live smoke proof, and retain the coordinated cleanup when every removed surface is confirmed private.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is connected to the merged dead-export ratchet and the coordinated browser/Codex cleanup history, making them the best available owner for the combined-scope decision.
